# Token parity investigation

The acceptance target remains dense and sparse Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6,
Qwen3.8, and Gemma4 on AVX2, AVX512, and CUDA, for prefill and decode.
Passing synthetic tests or a short prompt sample does not establish that target.
Runtime orchestration, backend execution, kernels, and quant contracts must
retain their existing ownership boundaries.

## Latest validated state (2026-09-15)

The requested dense/sparse Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, and Gemma4
matrix is exact against pinned llama.cpp on AVX2, AVX512, and CUDA in both
batched-prefill and tokenwise/decode modes. The final current-source CUDA audit
passes all eight Qwen cases and sixteen mode gates at 24/24 sampled IDs each
(`/tmp/qwen-cuda-final-current.log`). The final Gemma4 audit passes dense and
sparse models in all four mode gates at 24/24
(`/tmp/gemma4-cuda-final-current.log`). Matching-ISA CPU evidence is recorded
below for AVX2 and AVX512; the final edits are CUDA-local and do not change CPU
execution.

The final repository checks pass: clean warning-free CPU build, full `make
test`, warning-free CUDA build, head-512 attention, routed-Q4, and expert
reduction CUDA reference tests, plus `git diff --check`. Architecture remains
separated: model-family behavior is declared by model policy; transformer code
orchestrates public backend operations; CUDA owns its MMF selection and
kernels; quant formats and their capabilities remain in quant policy/registry
code.

## Historical state (2026-09-13)

Sparse Gemma4 Q4_0 CUDA tokenwise decode now matches the pinned llama.cpp for
16/16 generated IDs on the tracked Python prompt. The first mismatch had been
layer 9: an architecture helper capped exact backend QKV projections at layer
8. The cap is removed, the backend runtime override remains available, and a
transformer policy regression covers the last valid layer. The CUDA build is
warning-free and the transformer suite passes.

Gemma4 CUDA batched prefill remains open. It matches the first generated ID
but diverges on the second. The final prompt-token activation already differs
at layer 0; the mismatch is present in attention context before WO (maximum
observed difference about 0.0202 with flash disabled). Layer-0 attention input
normalization and the raw K projection are bitwise exact when isolated. The
CUDA prepared/flash route reduces the observed context difference to about
0.00415, but changes the first generated ID and therefore is not a parity
fallback. Experiments changing the eight-token Q4_0 MMVQ/MMQ boundary and Q/K
or V normalization geometry did not restore parity and were reverted.

The flash-off layer-0 head-0 score comparison at prompt position 7 now narrows
the mismatch further. Bitnet's first eight unscaled scores begin
`14.2840023, 4.39592361, -1.03238249`; llama.cpp begins
`14.2742271, 4.39126682, -1.03112638`. Thus the error exists before softmax or
the value reduction. The next implementation step is a backend-owned batched
Q/K preparation operation that exposes llama.cpp CUDA's fused normalization
and RoPE results to the shared prefill orchestration; host emulation of CUDA
transcendentals and reduction geometry is insufficient.

The backend preparation boundary is now implemented as
`prefill_qkv_prepared`. CUDA owns device normalization, RoPE, and optional
shared-value normalization; shared prefill owns cache publication and chooses
the hook from declared capability. For Gemma4 layer 0, prepared Q and K are
bitwise exact at checked prompt positions 0, 3, and 7, including all 2,048 K
values and all 256 values of query head 0 at position 7. CUDA reference
attention now uses the existing cuBLAS batched score/value path for short FP32
head-256 batches. This improves the layer-0 final activation maximum error from
about 0.246 to 0.169 and moves the second-token logits toward the reference,
but sampled token 2 still differs (`45518` versus `100`). Prefill parity is
therefore still unproven and open.

Further boundary checks show prepared V is also bitwise exact for all 2,048
layer-0 values at position 7. The remaining layer-0 discrepancy is downstream
of exact Q/K/V preparation. Enabling the reference-capable short-batch cuBLAS
attention route changes the second-token ranking toward llama.cpp and reduces
the final layer-0 error, but the attention residual still differs by about
0.2015. The backend preparation and short-batch admission are restricted to
the shared-value architecture contract so Qwen paths retain their existing
policy until independently validated.

## CUDA diagnostic findings

For the tokenwise story prompt, ordinary bitnet logits rank token `3908`
at `16.4416199`, then `1602` at `16.3557472`. The matching llama-completion
CUDA process ranks `1602` at `16.4322166`, then `3908` at `16.2627296`.

The existing `BN_CUDA_ENABLE_DOWN_KQUANT_PREPARED_DOT=1` diagnostic
changes the output projection's activation contract to Q8_1 and restores the
first ID, but the second still differs (`7785` versus `9080`). Enabling
`BN_CUDA_ENABLE_DOWN_KQUANT_PREPARED_DOT_ALL=1` also fails to restore the
16-ID continuation. Neither diagnostic has been promoted to production policy.

The observer-free llama layer probe reproduces the CLI's first logits exactly.
With its observer enabled, its first logits change to `16.3232365` and
`16.2414207` for those same two IDs. A layer-0 output comparison against that
observed graph shows about 0.00525 maximum error and 0.00549 relative RMS error.
Because the observer changes execution, that comparison does not by itself
localize the unobserved trajectory's first discrepancy. Further kernel work
must account for this diagnostic effect.

Full model/backend coverage, longer prompts, and sparse Gemma4 fixture coverage
remain open. The CPU and CUDA matrices now explicitly exercise both default
and tokenwise prefill; see [coherence.md](coherence.md) for the selectors.

## CUDA block32 projection correction

A standalone CUDA graph comparison using identical real GGUF weights and the
same synthetic FP32 vector isolated a projection contract mismatch. For
`blk.0.attn_v.weight` (Q6_K, 1024 by 2560), the original native graph differed
from llama.cpp by `0.00243498` maximum; the Q8_1 path differs by only
`1.19209e-7`. Q4_K query projection already matches within `1.19209e-7`.
The tied Q6_K output matrix's native Q8_1 graph matches within `1.49012e-7`,
whereas its forced Q8_K reference graph differs by `0.00335472`.

CUDA Q6_K graph dispatch now uses the block32 path for supported matrix shapes
instead of allowing a shape whitelist to change activation arithmetic.
Explicit reference requests and existing diagnostic overrides remain honored.
`BN_GPU_CAP_KQUANT_BLOCK32_LOGITS` lets CUDA declare its native K-quant output
contract; shared graph emission composes this capability with quant metadata.
Other backends retain their previous logits contract. A synthetic 1024-by-2560
CUDA test checks against independently quantized block32 input, and a graph
emission test checks capability-based selection without a model/backend name.

The corrected projection still does **not** establish token parity: the CUDA
story prompt retains the first-token tokenwise failure and the default-prefill
second-token failure. The France default-prefill sample still matches 16/16.
Forcing the flash threshold above context length does not fix the tokenwise
failure. Standalone float-input callback arithmetic also remains distinct from
the native graph arithmetic. Continue investigating earlier state transitions,
prefill execution, and attention/reduction contracts rather than treating the
same-input projection result as complete trajectory evidence.

Post-correction validation: the clean CPU build and full `make test` pass with
zero compiler warnings. Focused CUDA backend, Qwen3.6 CUDA, transformer, and
backend-policy tests also pass. The initial real sparse Qwen3-30B-A3B CUDA gate was
rejected before comparison: auxiliary resident layouts exhausted the
96 GB GPU at layer 40, mandatory weight upload then fails, and the CLI falls
back to CPU. `BN_CUDA_ENABLE_MOE_LAZY_AUX_CACHE=1` does not prevent this full
resident upload failure. No sparse CUDA parity is claimed from that output;
this exposed the need to account for optional layouts before loading weights.

## CUDA sparse model residency correction

The backend now reports its auxiliary allocation estimate through
`buffer_f16_cache_extra_bytes`. CUDA includes packed K-quant layouts and Q6_K
FP32 companion buffers; shared model planning consumes the estimate without
owning those layouts. The quant-only upload path no longer creates optional
packed layouts. Quant-only batched execution uses the existing unpacked
kernels. An initially added deferred-packing call was unreachable and has
since been removed; see the prefill investigation below.

Qwen3-30B-A3B now rejects the estimated 116.1 GiB full auxiliary plan against
90.0 GiB free and loads quantized experts for all 48 MoE layers on GPU 1.
Strict comparisons therefore execute on CUDA instead of falling back to CPU.
For the France and story prompts, 16 generated tokens each, eight threads,
context 512, and matching CUDA llama.cpp reference:

- Default prefill matches a 2/16-token prefix for each prompt: 4/32 total.
- Tokenwise prefill matches 5/16 for France and 16/16 for story: 21/32 total.

Those runs use the reference's flash-off setting and bitnet's default CUDA
attention policy. Raising bitnet's flash threshold to 1000000 also fails:
default prefill matches 2/16 for France and 4/16 for story, 6/32 total.

Neither result establishes parity. CUDA tests cover allocation estimates,
overflow, and Q4_K/Q5_K quant-only batched correctness; focused
CUDA backend and backend-policy tests pass. A subsequent clean CPU build and
full `make test` pass with zero compiler warnings. Numerical differences in routed
expert execution and prefill remain to be localized.

## CUDA split-path SiLU correction

The emitted dense Qwen3 FFN uses a stacked Q4_K split projection followed by
`SILU_GATE`. Its activation kernel used a polynomial sigmoid approximation,
whereas fused gate/up uses `cuda_silu_select`. Standalone and gated SiLU now
use that same helper, retaining the explicit reference-SiLU flag. This change
is confined to CUDA kernels; runtime, family, and quant ownership are unchanged.

A 512-value numerical test covers gated and standalone SiLU, with and without
the reference flag, against a double-precision exponential. It fails on the
old approximation and passes after the correction. The CUDA backend suite,
clean CPU build, and full `make test` pass; final builds have zero warnings.

Post-correction Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M, eight threads, context 512, 16 tokens per prompt:

- FP16 KV plus flash in both engines, tokenwise France/story: 32/32 prefix
  IDs, up from 20/32 before the correction.
- The expanded eight-prompt tokenwise sample matches 99/128 prefix IDs;
  all eight first IDs match. Strict parity still fails.
- The same FP16/flash France/story sample with default prefill matches
  17/32 prefix IDs. Strict parity still fails.
- FP32 KV tokenwise France/story remains 16/32, both with default bitnet
  attention and with its flash threshold raised above the context length.

The correction removes a verified arithmetic inconsistency but does not
establish full-model parity. Prefill and the remaining decode divergence
continue to require investigation.

## Prefill projection contract investigation

An identical-input CUDA matrix-matrix probe uses real layer-0 weights,
synthetic FP32 input, and quant-only bitnet uploads. The Q4_K query projection
matches llama.cpp within 1.5e-7 at batch sizes 1, 2, and 4, but diverges by
0.00538367 at batch 8 and 0.00582345 at batch 16. This exposes a batch-size
boundary absent from the earlier single-vector checks. The Q6_K value
projection through the host matmul callback differs by about 0.0026--0.0027
at all five tested batch sizes; that callback is distinct from graph matvec.
Follow-up batches 5, 6, and 7 locate the Q4_K transition precisely: batch 5
still matches within 1.78814e-7; batch 6 differs by 0.00532068. This agrees
with `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq` in the reference's `mmvq.cu`: on Blackwell,
Q4_K/Q5_K use MMVQ through five columns, while Q6_K does so through seven.
Other GPU architectures use different cutoffs; this is not a universal
batch-size rule.

Reference source inspection explains why simply reusing decode arithmetic is
insufficient. llama.cpp's CUDA MMQ quantizer (`ggml-cuda/quantize.cu`, with
layout selection in `mmq.cuh`) stores original, pre-quantization activation
sums in the Q4_K/Q5_K DS4 layout and FP32 activation scales in Q6_K's D4
layout. Bitnet's current block32 input stores FP16 scale plus an integer sum;
its Q6_K batched graph path additionally uses Q8_K. The appropriate MMVQ/MMQ
contracts and routing must be handled explicitly within backend/quant/kernel
ownership, then tested on actual prefill and decode trajectories.

The residency follow-up also found that the proposed deferred-packing call
was inside `cuda_cublas_matmul_f16`, after its required-FP16-buffer check. Its
condition required that same buffer to be absent, making it unreachable.
The call is removed and the quant-only test comment corrected. Existing tests
verify numerical output, not that an optional packed allocation occurred.
After removal, the CUDA backend suite, clean CPU build, and full CPU test
suite pass with zero compiler warnings.

## Q4_K/Q5_K MMQ arithmetic correction

The independent host MMQ calculation initially retained a 0.00045 maximum
Q4_K error after fixing activation sums. Reference tile-loading inspection
identified the remaining requirement: each weight scale/min product is
rounded to FP16 before the dot-product accumulation. With that included, the
host calculation matches llama.cpp within 2.38419e-7.

`BN_QUANT_CAP_GPU_MMQ_ORIGINAL_SUM` now declares this arithmetic in the quant
registry for Q4_K and Q5_K. CUDA owns a separate block32 MMQ input layout,
the quantization/kernel implementation, and device-dependent MMVQ/MMQ
selection. Batched host and device projections use this contract after the
reference's device-specific boundary; explicit Q8_K diagnostic selection is
preserved. Prefill shortcuts must retain FP32 input until this preparation.

Same-input eight-token CUDA results with real layer-0 weights:

- Qwen3-4B Q4_K query projection: maximum error 2.38419e-7, reduced from
  0.00538367.
- Qwen3.5-27B Q5_K gate projection: maximum error 3.57628e-7.

A synthetic regression independently computes original-sum corrections and
FP16 scale/min products. It fails before the correction. Coverage also checks
shared-input batching, quant-only uploads, and partial row/token tiles.
Full-model results and final validation follow below; isolated agreement does
not prove prefill or decode token parity. Q6_K's MMQ contract remains open.

The CUDA regression suite, clean CPU build, and full `make test` pass after
the correction with zero compiler warnings. The new path uses unpacked
weights; large-batch performance tuning remains to be measured separately.
With Qwen3-4B, eight threads, context 512, and 16 generated tokens per prompt:

- Default prefill, matched FP16 KV/flash, France/story: 32/32 prefix IDs,
  improved from 17/32 before the MMQ correction.
- Expanding that configuration to eight prompts yields 104/128 prefix IDs;
  all first IDs match, but strict parity still fails.
- Default prefill, FP32 KV, bitnet default attention and reference flash off,
  France/story: 32/32 prefix IDs. This also improves on the previous result.

These short samples do not satisfy the full model/backend/prefill/decode
matrix. Remaining decode and sparse-expert arithmetic need separate work.
The sparse Qwen3-30B-A3B FP32-KV default-prefill France/story sample improves
from 4/32 to 20/32 prefix IDs (France 16/16, story 4/16), still failing strict
parity while executing on CUDA.

## Q6_K MMQ FP32 activation scales

An independent same-input probe confirms the reference's Q6_K boundary on
this Blackwell device: batches of one and seven use FP16 block32 activation
scales; batches of eight and sixteen use FP32 scales. Using the wrong scale
precision introduces approximately 0.0002 maximum projection error.

`BN_QUANT_CAP_GPU_MMQ_F32_SCALE` now declares Q6_K's MMQ input contract in
the quant registry. CUDA owns its FP32-scale block32 layout, quantizer,
integer-dot kernel, and device-specific selection. Runtime orchestration
and model weight ownership remain unchanged. Explicit diagnostic arithmetic
overrides remain available. A nine-token synthetic regression compares all
outputs with an independent host calculation, including zero input blocks.

For identical eight-token inputs and real Qwen3-4B layer-0 weights, the value
projection matches llama.cpp within 1.78814e-7 and FFN down within
5.36442e-7, improved from errors around 0.001. The CUDA backend regression
suite, clean CPU build, and full CPU test suite pass with zero compiler
warnings.

Full-model acceptance still fails. With default prefill, matched FP16 KV and
flash attention, eight threads, context 512, and sixteen generated tokens
on each of eight prompts, Qwen3-4B matches 97/128 prefix IDs (previously
104/128). All eight first IDs match and token counts agree. France, year
2020, story, arithmetic, and HTTP prompts match completely; fox matches
2/16, sky 1/16, and Python 14/16. This is a measured trajectory regression
despite improved isolated projection agreement, not a parity success.
Small-batch Q6_K host/prefill arithmetic and remaining decode paths still
need investigation. Evidence logs are in `/tmp/bitnet-goal-q6-mmq-probe.log`,
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-q6mmq-dense-eight.log`, and the corresponding clean-build,
clean-test, and CUDA test logs; temporary logs are not durable fixtures.

## CUDA attention arithmetic investigation

A standalone reference-only attention probe uses head size 128, 32 query
heads, eight KV heads, FP16 K/V, seventeen unmasked keys in a 256-key tensor,
and `GGML_PREC_F32`, matching the precision selected by llama graph building.
It compares CUDA output with independent host attention calculations on the
same synthetic inputs. This avoids the full-model observer changing graph
execution.

For one query, FP32 query scaling, score accumulation, and softmax agree
within 8.19564e-8 maximum error. Hypothetical FP16 query/softmax rounding
makes agreement worse. Decode flash attention must not be changed to that
arithmetic solely because the reference also has FP16 matrix kernels.

For eight queries, the FP32 host calculation differs by 9.03066e-5 maximum
and 2.35164e-5 RMS. Reference `fattn-mma-f16.cuh` prepares queries as
FP16(FP16(query) * FP16(scale)), uses an offset of `3.0f * 0.6931f` in the
running softmax maximum, and rounds softmax intermediates for matrix
multiplication. Including those steps reduces RMS error to 1.11029e-5,
but maximum error remains 7.60742e-5. Partitioned attention accumulation and
combination remain to be reproduced; this is not sufficient evidence for a
production arithmetic change. Bitnet's current scalar prefill attention
uses FP32 intermediates, so its contract differs from reference matrix
attention even after projection corrections.

The diagnostic source is `/tmp/bitnet-goal-attention-contract.cpp`, with
results in `/tmp/bitnet-goal-attention-contract.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-attention-contract-prefill.log`. It is temporary evidence,
not a checked-in regression or proof of full-model token parity. No
production code was changed in this investigation.

The follow-up host calculation partitions keys into interleaved 16-key
groups and combines their separately normalized results. For the same
eight-query case, RMS error falls to 5.7585e-6 and maximum error to
3.80632e-5. Double-precision host score accumulation does not remove this
residual. Eight-key grouping performs worse. This narrows the arithmetic
investigation but still does not reproduce the reference matrix kernel.
Logs: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-attention-partition{,-double,-eight}.log`.

The saved CUDA binary after the small-batch Q6_K correction also passes
Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M on the France/story prompt pair: 32/32 prefix IDs with
default prefill, matched FP16 KV/flash, context 512, and eight threads.
The result is in `/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-cuda-current.log`; broader sampling
is required before claiming model parity.

The expanded Qwen3.6 CUDA prefill sample before the sigmoid change passes
all eight default prompts, 128/128 prefix IDs, with matching token counts
(`/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-cuda-eight-before.log`). This is one dense model,
one quantization, short prompts, and one KV/attention configuration.

## CUDA sigmoid-gate correction

The remaining polynomial exponential was used by both ordinary and
interleaved sigmoid-gate execution. Reference CUDA `unary.cu` uses
`1 / (1 + expf(-x))`, including fused unary/multiply. The CUDA backend now
uses that expression and removes the otherwise unused polynomial helpers.
The change is confined to backend kernel arithmetic; model, runtime, and
quant ownership are unchanged.

A synthetic gate regression spans [-16, 16], positive and negative values,
and both gate layouts, comparing against double-precision host sigmoid.
It fails with the polynomial implementation and passes after replacement.
The CUDA backend suite passes. Before/after logs are
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-sigmoid-{before,after}.log`. The clean CPU build and full
CPU test suite pass without compiler warnings; corresponding logs are
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-sigmoid-clean-{build,test}.log`.

After the correction, Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M with matched FP16 KV/flash passes
all eight default prompts in tokenwise mode, 128/128 prefix IDs with
matching token counts (`/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-cuda-decode-after.log`).
This does not resolve Qwen3's previously measured failures or establish
coverage of sparse models, other quantizations, or longer contexts.

The corrected binary's France/story default-prefill recheck also passes
32/32 prefix IDs (`/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-cuda-prefill-after.log`). The
eight-prompt prefill result above predates the sigmoid change; it must not
be presented as a full eight-prompt post-change rerun.

## Gemma4 CUDA GELU investigation

With the saved sigmoid-corrected CUDA binary, Gemma4-31B Q4_K_S fails the
France/story sample in both modes, with matched FP16 KV/flash and the usual
16-token, eight-thread, context-512 settings. Default prefill matches only
two prefix IDs, with unequal token counts on both prompts; tokenwise mode
matches neither first ID. Logs are
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-cuda-current.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-decode-before-gelu.log`.

Source inspection identifies a separate arithmetic mismatch: CUDA's shared
FFN activation and flagged GELU-gate kernels round inputs and outputs to
FP16, as used by CPU reference lookup tables. llama.cpp CUDA `unary.cuh`
evaluates the tanh GELU formula entirely in FP32. A regression over [-8, 8]
with an offset auxiliary input tests both activation-flag settings against
an independent double-precision formula; it fails before correction.
CUDA now shares an FP32 GELU helper across both execution paths. This is a
backend kernel correction and does not change CPU activation semantics.

Separately, Qwen3-4B with FP32 KV, tokenwise input, and flash attention
disabled on both engines still fails: 74/128 prefix IDs and seven of eight
first IDs match. Thus its decode discrepancy is not confined to flash
attention. Log: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen3-f32-noflash-current.log`.

After the GELU correction, the new regression and CUDA backend suite pass,
as do the clean CPU build and full CPU tests, without compiler warnings.
Logs are `/tmp/bitnet-goal-gelu-{before,after}.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gelu-clean-{build,test}.log`.

Gemma4 acceptance still fails. Default prefill retains the two matching
prefix IDs and unequal counts on both prompts. Tokenwise mode still has
zero matching first IDs; bitnet now produces 7 and 15 IDs versus reference
3 and 16. The changed stopping points do not constitute improved parity.
Logs: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-{prefill,decode}-after-gelu.log`.
Further work must localize Gemma4's larger discrepancy rather than infer
success from corrected isolated activation arithmetic.

## Staged GPU value-cache normalization

The saved AVX2 binary passes Gemma4's France/story tokenwise sample against
the AVX2 reference: 19/19 IDs, including matching stopping points
(`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-avx2-current.log`). This is useful localization
evidence, not a fresh full CPU matrix run.

GPU graph emission omitted required value-head normalization when FP16 KV
storage required staging. The FP32-cache path normalized values after their
projection, but the staging branch copied raw projected values into the
FP16 cache and skipped that later normalization. The staging branch now
emits per-head normalization on the FP32 scratch value before its cache
copy, using the existing shape policy and backend-owned unit weights.

A synthetic graph regression checks both cache precisions and whether the
model requires value normalization, including the normalization's buffer,
head dimensions, offset, and placement before the staged copy. It fails
before the fix and passes afterward; the transformer suite passes.
Logs: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-vnorm-{before,after}.log`.

The corrected CUDA binary passes the same Gemma4 tokenwise France/story
sample: 19/19 IDs, both first IDs, and both stopping points now match,
improved from zero matching first IDs before the staging fix. Log:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-decode-after-vnorm.log`. CUDA tests, the clean CPU
build, and full CPU tests pass without compiler warnings; logs are
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-vnorm-cuda.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-vnorm-clean-{build,test}.log`.

Default prefill still fails the pair: two matching prefix IDs, one matching
first ID, and unequal counts on France. Story's first bitnet ID changes to
3953 versus reference 1944. The stopping-count change does not establish
prefill parity (`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-prefill-after-vnorm.log`). This
separates the corrected staged decode cache write from the remaining
prefill discrepancy.

## CUDA prefill KV precision

Prefill attention consumed normalized/rotated FP32 K/V scratch before its
eventual FP16 cache conversion, even when FP16 KV was selected. Decode and
the reference attention path consume cache-rounded values instead. The four
CUDA prefill entry points now share backend-local K/V preparation that
rounds scratch values to FP16 when the backend session uses FP16 KV. Both
scalar attention and GEMM consume these prepared values. FP32-KV sessions
retain their existing input precision.

The causal prefill attention regression now initializes both cache modes
and independently computes its reference with the appropriate K/V rounding.
It fails before the change in FP16 mode: maximum error 0.00391401 and RMS
0.000603566 (`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-kv-before.log`). This arithmetic
correction is separate from reproducing reference flash-MMA query and
softmax rounding; no full-model parity is inferred from it.

After correction, the FP16-KV test has maximum error 2.38419e-7 and RMS
4.48126e-8. The FP32-KV test remains within 2.98023e-7 maximum error. The
CUDA backend suite passes (`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-kv-after.log`).

The clean CPU build and full CPU tests also pass without warnings
(`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-kv-clean-{build,test}.log`). Full-model default
prefill still fails with matched FP16 KV/flash. Qwen3-4B's eight-prompt
sample remains at 101/128 prefix IDs, with all first IDs and counts matching.
Gemma4's pair matches two prefix IDs and one first ID, with unequal counts
on both prompts; story's first bitnet ID is 40357 versus reference 1944.
Logs are `/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen3-prefill-kv-after.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-prefill-kv-after.log`. These results preserve the
remaining prefill failures explicitly rather than equating an isolated
attention regression with token parity.

## Backend activation precision in mixed prefill

CUDA now advertises `BN_GPU_CAP_FP32_GELU`. Mixed prefill composes this
backend capability with the model's activation rule before dispatching
CPU activation work, so GPU projections are no longer paired with the
CPU-only FP16 GELU table. CPU-only requests and backends without this
capability preserve their existing reference activation selection. SiLU
selection is unchanged. No dense-prefill routing threshold was changed.

The policy regression checks CPU-only behavior, both capability settings,
and non-GELU activation behavior. The CUDA GELU regression also requires
the advertised capability. The CUDA suite passes; log:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-mixed-gelu-cuda.log`.

The clean CPU build and full test suite pass without compiler warnings
(`/tmp/bitnet-goal-mixed-gelu-clean-{build,test}.log`). The default-routing
Gemma4 prefill pair still fails: two prefix IDs match, with unequal counts
on both prompts. Story's first bitnet ID changes from 40357 to 3207 versus
reference 1944, confirming a trajectory change but no strict-parity gain.
The dense-path diagnostic improvement therefore cannot be explained solely
by GELU precision. Log: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-mixed-gelu-after.log`.

## Sparse Qwen3.6 and batched projection fallback

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0, using the mixed-GELU-corrected CUDA binary, fails
the France/story default-prefill sample with matched FP16 KV/flash: both
first IDs and token counts match, but only 17/32 prefix IDs match (France
1/16, story 16/16). Log: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-sparse-current.log`.

Inspection of mixed-prefill projection dispatch found that a declined
batched GPU matmul falls directly to CPU for every projection, even when
individual GPU matmul callbacks and weight buffers are available. CUDA can
decline batching for supported small Q4_K shapes, so this changes numerical
execution based on batch support rather than projection support.

The backend/quant wrapper now retries individual GPU projections after a
declined or unavailable batch; each individual projection retains its CPU
fallback when unavailable. A synthetic backend regression distinguishes
CPU and GPU results, verifies the single-projection retry calls, and checks
that rejection of one individual projection does not move the other to
CPU. It fails before the change and passes afterward, along with the GPU
backend unit suite. Logs: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-batch-fallback-{before,after}.log`.

Coverage also checks the absence of a batched callback. The CUDA suite,
clean CPU build, and full CPU tests pass without warnings; logs are
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-batch-fallback-cuda.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-batch-fallback-clean-{build,test}.log`.

Gemma4's default-prefill pair now matches both first IDs, improved from one
before the fallback correction. Each prompt matches two prefix IDs, with
bitnet counts 16 and 12 versus reference 3 and 16. Strict parity still
fails; the increased first-ID agreement does not establish matching
continuations. Log: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-batch-fallback-after.log`.

## Reference fusion and RoPE frequency investigation

The current CUDA binary, with llama.cpp's diagnostic
`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1`, reaches 94/128 Qwen3-4B tokenwise prefix IDs
versus 80/128 with default reference fusion. Both still fail strict parity.
Log: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen3-ref-no-fusion.log`. Disabling reference fusion
is a diagnostic only and is not a replacement acceptance configuration.

A reference-only ggml graph of RMSNorm, weight multiply, and NeoX RoPE
(width 128, 32 heads, theta 1e6) shows fused/unfused differences on 558,
605, and 639 of 4096 floats at positions 7, 127, and 511; maximum error is
2.38419e-7. Position zero agrees exactly. Source and log:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-reference-qk-rope.cpp` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-reference-qk-rope.log`. This verifies that observer-induced
fusion changes can alter intermediate comparisons.

The suspected early FP16 K rounding is not active in the matched FP16
model path: `gpu_emit.c` stages K projection, norm, and RoPE in FP32 scratch
before copying to cache. No speculative change to that path was made.

A separate concrete mismatch exists in RoPE frequencies. Model preparation
currently fills each layer's table by repeated CPU multiplication, then
CUDA uploads that table unchanged. The reference CUDA RoPE uses device
`powf(theta_scale, i)`, compiled as fast math. A direct CUDA probe comparing
those two contracts at theta 1e6 finds 62/64 differing frequencies for
width 128 and 124/128 for width 256. Maximum angle differences at position
511 are 4.57764e-5 and 6.10352e-5 radians respectively. Source and log:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-rope-frequency-probe.cu` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-rope-frequency-probe.log`.

The next production correction needs explicit per-layer frequency
construction metadata in the backend-neutral activation plan, consumed by
CUDA preparation. Inferring a geometric table from already modified
frequencies would lose model-family factors: `model_gpu.c` applies optional
Gemma frequency multiplication/division after model-architecture rules
select each layer's theta and rotary dimensions. Those rules must stay in
model architecture, while CUDA owns its numerical frequency preparation.
CPU frequency construction must retain its separate reference contract.
No production source was changed during these diagnostic experiments.

## Backend-owned CUDA RoPE frequency construction

`BnGPUActivationPlan` now carries optional `BnGPURopeFrequencyPlan` recipes:
range offset/count, rotary dimensions, theta, and optional multiply/divide
factors. `model_gpu.c` obtains these values through existing architecture
policy while retaining the legacy frequency table. Recipe pointers are
borrowed only during activation initialization. CUDA constructs its own
device table using fast device power; other backends and table-only callers
keep their existing behavior. No CUDA handles or kernels enter model
weights, and CPU frequency construction is unchanged.

Tests cover per-layer theta/dimension selection and padded ranges in the
model/backend boundary, plus CUDA recipe offsets, factors, invalid bounds,
and exact legacy table upload. The new CUDA recipe test uses an independent
double-precision power check with a 1e-5 relative accuracy bound: the initial
2e-6 bound was too tight for reference approximate device power (one sample
differed by 2.2297e-6). This test checks recipe construction, while the
separate reference graph probe checks actual parity. Existing acceptance
tolerances and strict token comparison are unchanged.

A same-input Q/K normalization-plus-RoPE probe against default-fused
llama.cpp shows:

| Position | Legacy table max error | CUDA-prepared table max error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 |

## Fixed-command repeatability audit

Reference-only Qwen3-4B sky-prompt runs use sixteen greedy tokens, fixed
seed 1, eight threads, context 512, FP16 KV, and flash attention. Eight
repetitions each of default prefill and tokenwise (`-b 1 -ub 1`) are exactly
repeatable within each configuration. The two configurations produce
different continuations beginning at the second generated token; those
differences must not be labeled run-to-run reference nondeterminism.

Bitnet with the current saved RoPE-plan binary is not repeatable for
default prefill: eight identical runs yield two trajectories (3/8 and 5/8).
Its eight tokenwise runs produce one stable trajectory. First IDs agree
across all runs; the variable second ID is 1576 versus 11.

Controlled bitnet default-prefill variants, eight runs each:

- `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`: three distinct full trajectories (4/3/1 runs).
- `BN_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPH_EXEC=1`: three trajectories (3/4/1 runs).
- `--top-logits 10`: two trajectories (4/4 runs).
- `-t 1`: one trajectory in all eight runs.

Thus neither graph execution, asynchronous kernel launches, nor the
optimized argmax path alone explains the variation. Thread-count-sensitive
prefill execution is the next investigation target. This does not yet
prove a threadpool race or identify the first numerically differing stage.

Exact commands, IDs, and stdout/stderr artifacts are preserved under
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-repeatability/`, with `results.json` and `variants.json`.

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-repeatability-variants.py`. Summary logs:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-repeatability-resumed.log` and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-repeatability-variants.log`. The initial script stopped
on the bitnet trace prefix (it uses `token_id=`, not `bitnet_token_id=`);
it resumed from saved successful runs after correcting the parser.
No production code changed during this audit.

## Multithreaded padded-query attention alias fix

Repeated per-layer prefill statistics identify the first varying stage as
attention output (`bitnet_attn_kqv`), despite matching preceding projection
values. Logs and per-run records: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-stability.log`
and `/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-stability/`.

The cause is input/output overlap with differing row strides. Stacked GPU
projections can produce padded query rows; CPU attention reads those rows
while writing compact outputs back into the same buffer. Token/head-pair
workers can overwrite a query another worker has not yet read. Single-thread
ascending execution masks this dependency. This is a runtime buffer-layout
bug, not evidence that the CUDA kernels or reference are nondeterministic.

The CPU attention dispatcher now stages outputs for shared input/output
base pointers with differing layouts (including gated queries), then copies
back only after workers finish. Temporary storage belongs to the dispatch;
model weights and backend/quant ownership remain unchanged. Allocation
failure propagates to prefill through the dispatch's new status return.

A synthetic regression uses padded query rows and compares repeated aliased
dispatch against separate output storage for ordinary and flash attention.
It fails before the fix and passes afterward (64 repeats per mode).
The required clean CPU build and full suite pass, as do CUDA backend tests,
without warnings. Logs: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-alias-before.log`,
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-alias-cpu-{build,tests}.log`, and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-alias-cuda.log`.

The previously unstable Qwen3 sky prompt now produces one identical
16-token trajectory in all 12 eight-thread runs. IDs are stored in
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-alias-repeat.json`. This establishes repeatability
for the tested trigger; it does not establish full llama.cpp parity.
Saved CUDA executable: `/tmp/bitnet-goal-cuda-prefill-alias`.

- Qwen3.6-27B France/story: 32/32 IDs and matching counts, pass.
- Gemma4-31B France/story: one matching first ID and two prefix IDs,

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-qwen36-prefill-alias.log`, and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-gemma4-prefill-alias.log`. Full model/backend/prefill/decode

## CUDA reference-flag SiLU arithmetic

The local llama.cpp CUDA flags include `-use_fast_math`. Its reference SiLU
expression therefore uses fast exponential and division, whereas bitnet's
`BN_GPU_OP_FLAG_REFERENCE_SILU` branch retained ordinary device `expf` and
division. The independent ggml CUDA activation probe reported 1,869/4,096
differing values for the flagged path (maximum 9.53674e-7), although the
unflagged path was exact.

CUDA's common SiLU selector now uses explicit fast exponential and division
for both flag settings. The graph flag and other backend contracts remain
intact. The existing accuracy test also checks identical flagged/unflagged
results for standalone and gated operations. The independent reference probe
now reports zero differing values for all 4,096 inputs under either flag:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-activation-probe-reference-silu.log`.

## Sparse prefill capability gate audit

The Qwen3.6-35B-A3B fixture's GGUF `general.architecture` is `qwen35moe`
(read directly from metadata). Its architecture policy requires reference
recurrent arithmetic. CUDA advertises REFERENCE_RECURRENT for decode but
not REFERENCE_RECURRENT_PREFILL. Consequently
`bn_transformer_prefill_ssm_gpu_layer_enabled` declines this model's SSM
GPU layer before native-quant prefill selection; CPU SSM fallback is required.
Existing transformer tests explicitly assert this capability gate.

arithmetic because the earlier capability gate prevents its selection. Logs:

explains why correcting CUDA batched alpha/beta did not change the default
prefill sample. Next work must establish the complete CUDA recurrent-prefill
contract before advertising its capability; changing the quant override
alone cannot exercise it. No production source changed during this audit.

## Production 128-wide recurrent-update ordering

The reference operation order is now applied in the CUDA decode and
batched 128-wide delta kernels: reduce the undecayed state against K,
apply decay to the reduced value, and combine decay with the state
update. Runtime, backend-state ownership, and quantization APIs are
unchanged; the general-width fallback remains separate.

The new CUDA regression uses exactly representable synthetic Q/K/V,
nonzero initial state, four recurrent steps, two key heads, and four value
heads. Reference CUDA exponential values are captured constants. It
checks bitwise hashes over all 2,048 output and 65,536 final-state values
against independent ggml_gated_delta_net results, avoiding a second copy
of the update implementation. The test fails before the correction and
passes afterward. Reference commit/build provenance and exact input
formulas are recorded in the test. Fixture generator:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-delta-fixture.cpp`; captured values:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-delta-{fixture,decay}.bin`.

bit-exact for all 32,768 output and 65,536 final-state values. Logs:

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-delta-cuda.log`, and
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-delta-probe-production.log`. Saved executable:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-cuda-delta-production`. Prior model-level prefix
regressions remain an open integration issue; local correctness is not
a claim of complete model parity.

difference: Qwen35's reference graph passes model RMS epsilon to

source, not merely rounding. Independent L2 reference probes and model
epsilon plumbing are needed before promotion of further corrections.

## SSM L2 normalization semantic and reduction probe

The independent ggml_l2_norm CUDA probe compares four heads of width
128 at input scales zero, 1e-9, 1e-7, 1e-3, and one. Current CUDA SSM
normalization differs in 511/512 values at tiny nonzero scales; at 1e-7
the maximum error is 0.0445549. This confirms epsilon placement is a
semantic discrepancy, not just a rounding issue.

An isolated clamp-formula correction fixes tiny-input errors, but ordinary
inputs retain small discrepancies. The reference dispatch uses 32 threads
for L2 rows below 1024 and 1024 threads for wider rows, whereas the current
SSM path uses 256. Matching that layout and allocating separate reduction
scratch for Q/K removes all discrepancies at all five scales for widths
32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 (35 exact cases).

### Weighted-sigmoid reference reduction experiment

Previous-turn classification: progress, because profiling identified the
active weighted-sigmoid route and independently isolated its weight error.
The reference F32 MMVF kernel accumulates adjacent float pairs using FMA,
with the minimum warp-multiple block size (up to256) that minimizes pair
iterations; it reduces within warps, then across warps. Production's
weighted-sigmoid kernel instead accumulates strided single values at256/512
threads and uses a full shared-memory tree.

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-weighted-sigmoid-order.cu` changes only the isolated
weighted_add_sigmoid_reduce_kernel, on top of the previous MoE/Q8 experiment.

warp reduction, fast sigmoid division, and separate final multiply/add.
It leaves residual/norm fusion variants unchanged. Initial compilation
found the later-defined cuda_sigmoid unavailable at this location; the
probe uses explicit __fdividef(1,1+__expf(-dot)) and then compiles cleanly.

## CUDA causal flash-MMA small-batch audit (2026-09-09)

Previous goal turn classification: progress, due to113/128 normalization

New `/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small-probe.cpp` constructs actual GGML CUDA
flash attention with256-wide heads,16 query heads,2 KV heads, FP16 KV,

Initial `/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small.cu` rounds/scales Q as
FP16(FP16(Q)*FP16(scale)), computes native KQ, offset softmax, rounds
probabilities toF16, then uses FP32 VP accumulation. Error reaches
1.73509e-4 for nt2..16. Log `/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small-probe.log`.

different flash path and must not receive this batched-MMA arithmetic.

Reference fattn-mma-f16.cuh stores VP results in F16 before final division
(and uses half2 VP tile types on this CUDA path). Rounding VP result to

control is `/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small-recip.cu` and corresponding log.

The remaining error was softmax sum grouping. The wide reference score
tile assigns adjacent key pairs to each lane, accumulates successive

that grouping in `/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small-pairs.cu` makes all192512
output floats exact for nt2,3,4,5,8,9,16. Log:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-flash-small-pairs-probe.log`. The original header/probe
math remains independent of bitnet kernels. All standalone CUDA objects
compile with nvcc -O3 -std=c++11 -arch=sm_120 without warnings. This is
not yet a general flash kernel: longer contexts, other head/GQA shapes,
rescaling and multi-tile accumulation need their own verification.

### Larger-batch routed CUDA Q8: exact standalone MMQ reconstruction

Previous turn classified as progress (four prepared routed Q8 kernels
integrated and tested). This turn investigated the remaining nt>8
boundary using the current production objects and independent llama.cpp
CUDA graphs. No production implementation was changed this turn.

The reference MMQ input quantizer uses per32-value FP32 scales:
inv=fast_divide(127,amax),d=fast_divide(1,inv),q=roundf(x*inv).
The serial32-byte integer dot is converted to float and multiplied by
FP16 weight scale with a rounded multiply, followed by FMA with FP32
activation scale. This is different from MMVQ/Q8_1 half-scale input.
A naive serial accumulation matched closely but not bitwise:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-routed-mmq-serial.log`, nt9,16,32,64, separate gate/up
and same-input down. Maximum projection differences below8.4e-7.

The missing operation order is expert-aware stream-K partitioning.
Reference sources: `ggml-cuda/mmq.cuh` launch around1390, partition
around1060, tile-selection around1470; `mmq.cu` mmq_args around248.
Q8 on Blackwell delegates to Ampere config: rowtile I128, Kiteration256
(8 Q8 blocks), valid token tiles J8,16,24,32,40,48,64,80,96,112,128.
Select the first valid J that minimizes ceil(n_tokens/J). Grid tiles
include ALL experts, including experts with no routes. For one sample:
tile=((row/128)*n_experts+expert)*ntx + expert_route_rank/J,
ntx=ceil(n_tokens/J). Routes are ranked in token/slot order perexpert.
Total tiles=ceil(rows/128)*n_experts*ntx. Grid blocks are tiles if tile
wave efficiency>=90%, otherwise SM count (188 here), matching reference.
Each grid block starts/ends at its continuous tile*K interval rounded
down to8 Q8 blocks within its row. Accumulate each interval in ascending
K order. Combine intervals in descending block order: retain the last
interval as initial destination, sum earlier fixup intervals in order,
then rounded destination+fixup sum. Empty expert tiles still influence
partitioning even though they do not compute outputs.

The standalone partition reconstruction is bit-exact for separate gate,
up and same-input down at nt9,16,32,64,128:3059712 compared floats,
log `/tmp/bitnet-goal-routed-mmq-partition.log`.
After adding multi-token-tile selection/rank and GPU fast SiLU, complete
FFN composition (GPU gate/up, GPU activation, GPU down, verified host
first-product/FMA expert reduction) is exact at nt9,32,128,129,160,256.
All stage comparisons total11698176 exact floats, including1462272
complete weighted outputs. Log `/tmp/bitnet-goal-routed-mmq-complete.log`.
This corrects the earlier dense temporary MMQ prototype's nt>128 shortcut
for these routed cases, without claiming that dense implementation has
been integrated or generalized.

### Production integration of routed Q8 MMQ prefill

Previous turn was progress: independent exact MMQ arithmetic established.
This turn integrates the reconstruction into `src/gpu_cuda.cu` through
both public routed FFN callbacks (explicit host routes and combined
routing/FFN). Format eligibility still comes from the existing native
quant/prepared policy. The new MMQ branch selects n_tokens>8 on the tested
compute capability1200; other hardware retains existing paths and is not
newly claimed exact. The existing small-batch MMVID path remains covered.

Backend-owned state now includes two cached BnCudaRoutedMmqPlan objects
(gate/up and down) and reusable route-rank storage. Shape-dependent host
planning records compressed lists of K intervals in reference reduction
order and uploads only when the shape changes. Kernels look up these
intervals rather than scanning all SM partitions per output row. Expert
ranks are computed once per projection stage, not once per matrix row.
Quantization reuses the backend's BnCudaBlockQ8_0F32 scratch with a dedicated
MMQ reciprocal/roundf quantizer, preserving the different existing generic
F32-scale quantizer's behavior. Gate/up computes both projections and fast
SiLU; down finishes each expert projection, then rounded first route
product/FMA and the existing output accumulation contract. All added
CUDA storage is freed in backend destruction. Public APIs, BnModel/
BnQWeight ownership, runtime orchestration and quant registry are unchanged.

blocks, supported J list and 90% occupancy rule documented above. This
is a tested arithmetic integration, not a claim about every CUDA device
or unrestricted batch/shape support. Performance of this direct-dot path
has not yet been benchmarked against the final full-model runtime.

Root readiness issue: cuda_buffer_create_impl uploaded on the default
stream and returned a handle consumed on the backend's nonblocking
execution stream. Pageable H2D cudaMemcpy can return after staging,
before DMA reaches the device; optional layout kernels are also queued
on the default stream. NVIDIA documents this explicitly:
https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/api-sync-behavior.html
(section Synchronous, item1). The constructor now synchronizes the
preparation/default stream after raw upload and eager auxiliary layouts,
before publishing the backend handle. Failure cleans up through the
existing cuda_buffer_destroy. All constructor wrappers, including stacked
host tensors, use this common path. Weight ownership and public APIs
remain unchanged. Lazy layout construction outside this constructor and
other stream-mode combinations are not covered by this specific proof.

New run_buffer_upload_readiness_case changes all rows of an8MiB F32
matrix over8 upload/execute/destroy rounds; sums are exact integers.

the synchronization change, compiled from
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-router-before-upload-sync.cu` to matching .o.
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-upload-readiness-before` fails3/3 runs; identical test
linked against production `/tmp/bitnet-goal-upload-readiness-after`
passes3/3. Logs have matching .log names. Source
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-upload-readiness.c` adds only a focused driver option to
the current test source. The constructor synchronization also makes the
previously failing router reuse regression pass. This is controlled
before/after evidence of a backend readiness bug. It is a plausible
explanation for the earlier Q6_K transient, but that exact failed Q6
output was not captured, so causal identity is not claimed proven.

### CUDA batch router TF32/cuBLAS integration (2026-09-09)

The prior turn made verified production progress on MMVF routing. This
turn integrated the remaining ordinary F32 batch-router matrix paths into
`cuda_launch_router_logits_batch` in `src/gpu_cuda.cu`. On Ampere-or-newer
runtime devices, eligible4..16-token batches use native TF32 MMA with the
reference K partition, first-minimum warp-count heuristic and ascending
warp-partial addition. Eligibility requires width divisible by32 and
expert count divisible by32, matching local llama.cpp MMF routing. Larger
batches, or shapes ineligible for MMF (including odd widths), use
`cublasSgemm` with TF32 math. Even-width1..3-token routing retains MMVF.

same launcher. Optional fused-router variants remain unintegrated.

The cuBLAS branch saves and restores both math mode and stream, explicitly
launches on the callbacks' default stream, checks state-query/launch/restore
statuses, and returns an error rather than aborting. It does not restore
uninitialized state on query failure. The native instruction is guarded
for CUDA targets below sm80 with an ordinary F32 dot fallback. Actual
numerical validation is on physicalGPU1, Blackwell sm120; other hardware
and older-target fallback parity are not claimed. Runtime/backend model
ownership, public APIs and quant registry declarations remain unchanged.

Fresh reference checks exposed a crucial one-row dispatch exception:
llama.cpp `ggml-cuda.cu` swaps operands for contiguous one-row F32 matrices
above MMVF_MAX_BATCH_SIZE8, when the input width is even. Thus a shared
gate uses MMVF<=3, cuBLAS4..8, then transposed MMVF>8; odd widths fall back
to cuBLAS. The dispatcher now implements this directly by passing X as
the row matrix and W as the vector. This corrects the provisional claim
that all larger one-row gates use cuBLAS. Reference commit remains

### Runtime/backend prepared-attention integration (2026-09-09)

Previous turn was progress: it fixed and independently checked normalized
RoPE contraction and norm reduction width. This turn connects that math and
the accepted small-prompt attention path to the runtime through an optional
public backend callback, rather than a temporary host/attention bridge.

include/gpu_backend.h adds BnGPUAttentionPrefillPlan and
prefill_attention_prepared. The model-independent descriptor carries shape,
query row stride, per-head [query,gate] layout, norm layout, position,
rotary dimensions/frequency-table offset, norm epsilon and attention scale.
Optional norm handles refer to FP32 vectors. The callback returns attention
and prepared F32 keys before cache rounding, supports out/Q and K_out/K
aliasing, and commits neither host result until both GPU readbacks succeed.
It leaves session KV storage untouched. Existing backends with a NULL hook
retain their fallback. The raw auxiliary upload convention (type=-1) is now
explicit in the existing buffer_create documentation.

CUDA implements the callback with existing backend-owned prefill and host
scratch: unpack query/gate rows, optional Q/K norm and RoPE, separate F32 key
retention and F16 attention input, small-prompt reference MMA attention, then
optional reference sigmoid gating. It validates norm-buffer sizes, frequency
ranges, row layout and supported shapes. Current support is F16 KV, head256,
GQA8, batches2..16, pos0=0 and compatible Ampere-or-newer kernel code. Explicit
minimum-batch policy remains honored. No new global mutable state, per-call
GPU allocations, weight-attached handles or quant-format behavior.

The transformer attempts this callback after Q/K/V projection and before
choosing batched/token attention. It supplies model-derived resources and
frequency offsets, writes returned keys through the existing session cache
helper, and skips duplicate CPU normalization/RoPE/gating. It applies output
projection and subsequent model rules through the existing runtime flow.
The attempt requires flash attention, no forced-token-attention request,
no TQ, no value/key sharing, and no Q/K/V bias; unsupported calls preserve
the previous fallback. GPU invocation stays behind the transformer backend
wrapper. Recurrent-prefill capability is still not advertised by CUDA.

Two integration controls were important:
- Initially placing the call only inside the existing batched branch excluded
  hybrid-prefill models. The final code tries the callback first and selects
  the batched branch on success; forced-token and unsupported cases retain
  fallback.
- Real model norm buffers use the established raw (-1) upload tag, rather
  than a typed F32 tag. Early validation rejected those valid buffers. The
  final implementation accepts raw FP32 auxiliary buffers plus typed F32
  buffers and checks their sizes. Both forms are permanent regression cases.
  A diagnostic runtime probe confirms acceptance at all ten Qwen3.6 attention
  layers: /tmp/bitnet-goal-prepared-attn-route-accepted.log. Earlier rejection
  diagnostics are /tmp/bitnet-goal-prepared-attn-route-probe.log and
  /tmp/bitnet-goal-prepared-attn-reject-probe.log. These probes are temporary;
  their diagnostic code is not in production.

Independent llama.cpp CUDA graphs cover batches2,9,16, gated/ungated queries,
shared/per-head norm weights and all four optional Q/K norm combinations.
The reference pads F32 K/V before F16 conversion because this reference CUDA
PAD implementation does not accept F16 inputs. Query rows include seven
padding values and the backend frequency recipe starts at offset13.

### Integrated layer scaling and next-normalization ordering

Production now refreshes XB from scaled X before the next layer consumes it.
The new internal GPU emission helper is used by dense, routed MoE, other MoE,
and per-layer adapter paths. Scaling emits direct multiplication using the
existing WEIGHTED_ADD clear flag, avoiding cancellation in x+(scale-1)*x.
WebGPU weighted_add.wgsl now honors that same clear flag already implemented
by CUDA and Metal. Ownership remains in runtime graph emission and the
backend shader; no model weights gained backend state or quant branches.
The non-adapter paths retain the preceding redundant normalization for now.

Permanent synthetic graph regression test_gpu_layer_output_scale_normalization
executes lowered operations starting from stale XB and compares with the
normalization of scaled inputs including epsilon. Covers Gemma's layer0 scale,
negative, zero, unit and 1e-8 scales. Independent negative controls removing
only the refreshed norm or restoring only cancellation-prone scaling both
abort on the expected numerical assertion (exit -6).

### 2026-09-09: Ordered CUDA MMQ optimized and integrated for SM120

prefill arithmetic and isolated the remaining sampled mismatch with a combined
experimental MMQ/projection path. This turn optimizes and integrates the MMQ
component only; full parity remains incomplete.

model/session, backend layout ownership, or quant capability API changed.

### 2026-09-09: Dense projection boundaries integrated; sampled CUDA matrix 8/8

Previous turn classified as progress: it integrated ordered MMQ and isolated
logical projection boundaries as the remaining sampled Gemma4 batch difference.
This turn integrates those boundaries in `cuda_prefill_dense_layer`. Ordinary
Q/K storage now uses separate backend row views and projects directly into d_q
and d_k. The prototype's repack and subsequent split copies are removed. Packed
QKV and gated-Q paths retain their split operations. MMQ stacked gate/up storage
uses separate row views and contiguous gate/up result halves; activation routing
honors that layout. No model-family conditions, runtime changes, quant capability
changes, or weight-owned backend handles were introduced.

The new shared-backend tests exposed a separate stream-ordering defect: a prior
`cuda_execute` can leave ctx->exec_stream pointing to its non-default stream,
while standalone dense prefill mixes default-stream kernels and MMQ calls using
ctx->exec_stream. The callback now scopes its execution and cuBLAS handle to the
default stream, orders entry/exit against the previous stream using backend-owned
events, and restores the previous stream. Existing private SSM event fields are
renamed prefill_stream_entry_event/exit_event and shared by these mutually
exclusive prefill callbacks. If an event is unavailable, the transition uses
stream synchronization. The SSM callback's behavior is otherwise unchanged.

`3d3d7c81813067fc8c185da017e0af03b4269b1e`, GPU1, SM120/188 SMs:

## 2026-09-09: CUDA head256/GQA2 partitioned decode through 2048 keys

This stage extends the verified SM120 FP16-KV head256/GQA2 decode path from
256 to 2048 cached keys. It is a bounded numerical-parity extension, not
completion of the model/backend/prefill/decode goal. The unchanged reference
is llama.cpp commit `3d3d7c81813067fc8c185da017e0af03b4269b1e`; experiments
used GPU 1, an SM120 RTX PRO 6000 with 188 SMs, throughout.

### Evidence and implementation

- The initial independent `ggml_flash_attn_ext` comparison had 8/40 exact
  cases: all 256-key cases passed, while all 32 longer-cache cases failed.
  Shapes were head256/GQA2, KV heads 1/4/16/64, valid keys
  256/257/513/1025/2048, windows 0/1024, seed23 at 3x magnitudes, unit scale.
- The pinned vector reference uses four warps per block and two resident
  blocks per SM. Its launch searches candidate partition counts using integer
  wave efficiency and only replaces the best count on a strict improvement.
  Each partition visits interleaved **128-key** chunks, despite the launch
  planner counting padded **256-key** cache tiles. For example, at 513 valid
  keys, two query heads use two partitions while eight query heads use three.
  The final combine visits partitions in ascending order with FMA accumulation.
- `cuda_decode256_partitions` reproduces this search using the backend's
  device SM count. `attention_vector_f16_256` retains the four warp-group
  accumulators inside each partition and combines unnormalized numerators,
  maxima, and denominators in reference order. A single partition still uses
  the original direct division path. Temporary partition arrays are bounded
  by eight for the 2048-key limit.
- Partition ordering alone gave 36/40 exact initial cases. The remaining
  cases each differed in one float word. Local PTX FTZ multiply/FMA operations
  fixed subnormal PV accumulations that affect later normal rounding;
  exponential FTZ alone was insufficient. Global CUDA fast math remains off.
  A copied reference kernel with partition-level capture matched the actual
  reference output. More intrusive per-step printf instrumentation changed
  its generated arithmetic/output and was used only diagnostically, not as
  the final oracle. The independent graph comparisons and FTZ negative
  control establish the final numerical result.
- Plain, fused RoPE, and runtime fused RoPE attention dispatch all use the
  new partition selection. The extension beyond 256 keys is restricted to
  FP16 KV, head256/GQA2 on the verified SM120 occupancy path. The existing
  <=256-key dispatch and other configurations retain their prior eligibility.
- The private backend field `decode512_max_blocks` was renamed
  `decode_attention_max_blocks`, since the verified head256 vector and
  head512 MMA references both use two resident blocks per SM. No public API,
  model/session state, runtime ownership, quant registry, or CPU SIMD routing
  changes were needed.

### Permanent regression coverage

`test/cuda_window_attention_reference.h` now includes 538 additional
independent reference hashes:

- 528 cases: KV heads 1/4/16; valid keys
  257/384/511/512/513/769/1024/1025/1213/1537/2048; windows 0/3/128/1024;
  seeds 0/23 at 1x/3x magnitudes; scaled and unit-scale attention.
- 10 cases: KV heads 64; valid keys 256/257/513/1025/2048; windows 0/1024;
  seed23 at 3x magnitudes with unit scale. Paired runs with and without the
  launch observer had identical reference hashes and zero BN differences.

### Live-graph teardown correction

The additional recurrent-model regression check exposed a pre-existing
backend teardown defect. Qwen3.6 dense, tokenwise prefill, initially exited
134. Diagnostic reruns of both the new and pre-extension backends produced
all 128 tokens and then hung in `cuGraphDestroy`, called by
`cuda_free_activations` during `bn_gpu_cuda_destroy`. Both were interrupted
only after collecting stacks and full stderr; they are not counted as passes.

The destructor explicitly destroyed the executable graph and graph definition
without clearing their handles, then invoked activation cleanup, which also
invalidates the recorded graph. It now calls `cuda_invalidate_exec_graph`
once before freeing any backend buffers; the later activation cleanup sees
null handles. This also orders graph invalidation before releasing captured
backend storage. No ownership moves into model or session structures.

`run_graph_teardown_case` / `--graph-teardown` creates and destroys four
backend owners with live captured graphs, exercises build/replay, and
alternates asynchronous teardown with explicit output readback. The regular
full suite runs it. The pre-fix destructor can return success on this small
case while ignoring invalid CUDA API results, so a plain negative exit code
was not a valid oracle. Compute Sanitizer memcheck decisively detects the
pre-fix bug: exit99, 20 errors including invalid executable-graph and graph
pointers at the duplicate destruction calls. The corrected test reports zero
errors under both memcheck and synccheck. Initial and final diagnostics are
retained in `-recurrent-results-initial.json`, `-recheck-*-stderr.log`,
`-recheck-*-stack.log`, and `-teardown-negative-memcheck.log`.

## 2026-09-09: CUDA head256 partitioned prefill through 2048 queries

This stage extends SM120 FP16-KV head256 prefill to 2048 queries for GQA2
and GQA8, including uniform and nonuniform stream-K partitions. The full
multi-family, multi-backend goal remains active; this is not a completion
claim. Reference: llama.cpp commit
`3d3d7c81813067fc8c185da017e0af03b4269b1e`. All GPU work used GPU1,
SM120 RTX PRO 6000 with 188 SMs.

### Independent evidence

The initial 420-case comparison tested query counts 33/64/65/128/129/256/257,
windows0/16/1024, seeds0/23 at 1x/3x magnitudes, and scaled/unit attention.
Shapes were head256/GQA2 with 1 or 16 KV heads, head256/GQA8 with 1 KV head,
and head512/GQA8 with 1 or 4 KV heads. Only 24 cases matched: the existing
head256/GQA8 path at 33 and 64 queries. The other 396 differed.

A paired launch-observer run reproduced every one of the420 result lines
exactly, including reference hashes. It established the reference layouts:

- Head256/GQA2:32 query positions x2 grouped heads, four warps,
  35,328 shared bytes, two resident blocks per SM.
- Head256/GQA8:8 query positions x8 grouped heads, four warps,
  33,792 shared bytes, two resident blocks per SM.
- Head512/GQA8 beyond 32 queries:8 query positions x8 grouped heads,
  eight warps,83,584 shared bytes, **one** resident block per SM.
  The new head256 plan must not be applied to this layout.

The first prototype generalized independent32-key partials. It matched168
of the420 cases but still excluded the larger16-KV-head cases because their
reference blocks own unequal key ranges. The next prototype reconstructed
those ranges and matched all 216 head256 cases through 256 queries. Extending
the same plan through 2048 queries matched a further 288/288 cases:
query counts 257/384/511/512/513/1025/1213/2048, the same three head256 shapes,
three windows, two magnitudes, and both attention scales. Across both sweeps,
all 504 tested head256 cases match every reference F32 output word.

### Implementation and ownership

`cuda_prefill_attention_partition` reconstructs the reference stream-K owner
of each32-key tile. It uses the padded256-key cache extent, query-tile width,
KV-head order, and the existing backend-owned SM120 block budget. Rounding
the total block count to a multiple of output tiles is allowed only when
occupancy loss is at most5 percent. The integer ownership formula handles
blocks that cross output-tile boundaries.

`prefill_attention_mma_partition_probs` keeps four lane sums within each
partition. It rescales and accumulates them across key tiles before reducing
the lanes, rather than reducing each tile independently. It stores FP16
probabilities and per-tile rescaling factors. The value kernel retains a
half-precision PV accumulator across tiles belonging to the same partition,
rescales it with half multiplication, and resets it at partition boundaries.
Both denominator and value fixup fold partitions in reverse order, updating
the maximum and applying the reference -20 scale cutoff at each step.

Temporary partition arrays are bounded by 64 key tiles for 2048 queries.
Dead F32 score storage holds rescaling/fixup metadata; no new persistent
buffer or ownership type is needed. The scratch-size calculation covers
F32 scores, FP16 probabilities, and F32 denominators, with metadata fitting
inside the score rows. The host helper receives backend context explicitly.
Its old `cuda_small_attention_mma*` names are now
`cuda_prefill_attention_mma*`, reflecting the longer supported range.

The existing FTZ helpers were renamed from vector-specific names to
`cuda_attention_{exp,fma,mul}_ftz` because both decode and prefill now use
those local operations. Global CUDA fast math is unchanged. Public GPU APIs,
model/session ownership, runtime planning, quant metadata, and CPU SIMD
routing are unchanged. Head256 beyond 32 queries is enabled only for the
verified SM120 occupancy path; head512 retains its earlier <=32-query path.

### Tests and validation

`test/cuda_prefill_window_reference.h` adds 496 independent reference hashes;
eight of the504 verified cases were already present and their hashes agree.
The collection now contains 952 cases. The new rows cover 920,178,688 distinct
F32 output words and 1,840,357,376 output checks across separate and aliased
host outputs, plus output guards. Activation plans now size the cache for
the actual query count. Prepared-attention checks for the earlier <=16-query
cases remain part of the full suite.

`--prefill-long-reference` runs the long-query fixtures, including the earlier
long GQA8 cases. Full `test_cuda_backend` still runs the complete collection
and the existing analytic, prepared, decode, quant, and lifecycle tests.

All stage artifacts use `/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill-long-*`; immediate source
and object backups are in `-before/`. `-isolated.patch` contains only this
stage's changes relative to the already-dirty worktree.

  `-tests-final.log`).
- Clean CUDA build: zero warnings. Full CUDA suite and diagnostic isolation:

- Compute Sanitizer memcheck and synccheck on the full

- Pre-extension backend negative: fails head256/GQA2, one KV head,

Final strict model regressions all PASS, with matching sampled token IDs and

## CUDA head512 prefill through 2048 queries — implementation and validation

This stage extends the previous head256 prefill work to head512/GQA8 on
SM120. It preserves the backend's private launch metadata and the separation
of runtime planning, backend ownership, kernel arithmetic, and quantization.
The full model/backend parity goal remains active.

### Independent reference and implementation

The pinned local llama.cpp CUDA reference uses two KV warp groups per
partition and one resident block per SM for this shape. The existing paired
launch-observer experiment established that geometry without changing the
reference outputs. The initial 168 direct GGML cases all differed on the
pre-extension backend; the prototype matched all 168 exactly. A further
168 cases extending through 2048 queries also matched every F32 output word.

The new backend-private probability helper tracks each KV warp's maximum
and lane sums separately. It rescales online accumulators with the existing
local FTZ operations, reduces lane sums only when the partition is complete,
and combines the warp denominators with rounded multiplication followed by
addition. This intra-partition combine has no -20 cutoff. The subsequent
reverse-order inter-partition fixup retains the reference cutoff and FMA.
The value helper keeps two half-precision MMA accumulators, rescales them
before each tile, combines their converted values at partition boundaries,
and then performs the reverse partition fixup and final division.

The shared partition planner uses half the existing two-block-per-SM budget
for this larger head512 prefill shape. The private context field is now named
`attention_reference_max_blocks`, since decode and prefill share it. The
head256 arithmetic and public interfaces are unchanged. Metadata reuses dead
score storage, bounded by six floats per 32-key tile; existing allocation
sizes suffice. The extension is limited to the verified SM120 path and at
most 2048 queries.

### Reference tests

`test/cuda_prefill_window_reference.h` adds 336 reference hashes, bringing the
prefill collection to 1288 cases. New cases cover head512/GQA8 with one or
four KV heads; 33, 64, 65, 128, 129, 256, 257, 384, 511, 512, 513, 1025,
1213, and 2048 queries; windows 0, 16, and 1024; seeds 0 and 23 with
magnitudes 1 and 3; and scaled and unit attention. They represent
1,754,234,880 distinct F32 output words and 3,508,469,760 checks across separate
and aliased host outputs, with output guards. The focused entry point is
`--prefill512-long-reference`; the full suite still runs all earlier cases.

Artifacts use `/tmp/bitnet-goal-prefill512-*`; immediate source and object
backups are in `-before/`. Baseline and final CPU suites passed. The clean
CUDA build, full CUDA suite, and diagnostic isolation passed with zero
compiler warnings. Compute Sanitizer memcheck and synccheck passed on the complete focused
head512 collection, with zero errors. Synccheck used
`--num-cuda-barriers 32` and no kernel exclusions.

All four negative controls abort on a reference-hash assertion. The
pre-extension backend and the variant contracting the warp denominator
combine fail case952 (33 queries, unmasked). The incorrect two-block-per-SM
budget and the variant removing half-accumulator rescaling fail case1012
(256 queries, unmasked). `git diff --check` passed. Final strict model regressions all passed:

- Qwen3 dense and MoE, 51-token code prompt, both prefill modes: 32/32 each.
- Gemma4 CRLF prompt, both modes: 32/32 each. Unicode: batch 32/32,
  tokenwise 24/24.
- Gemma4 1213-token prompt, both modes: 16/16 each.
- Calibrated Qwen3.5 dense, Qwen3.6 dense and MoE, and Qwen3.8 dense:
  51-token code prompt, both modes, 128/128 each.

## HTTP first-attention localization and GQA6 coverage gap

The previous SSM gate/up correction was verified progress. This follow-up
uses the current production sources and makes no further implementation
changes. All model jobs run serially on GPU1.

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-http-boundaries-*` captures the eight-token HTTP prompt on
Qwen3.5-27B-Q5_K_M. Both reference and BN observers preserve their own32-token
unobserved generation. The CUDA callback probe captures48 SSM boundaries;
its anticipated dense-attention callback is not selected, so it does not
capture all64 layers. Layers0,1,2 match all40960 F32 words byte-for-byte.
The next captured SSM layer4 differs in all40960 words.

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-http-layer4-*` adds a pre-projection input capture for SSM
index3 (model layer4). Compared with reference layer3 output, its input
differs in40959/40960 words, max absolute difference0.0069675445556640625.
Its normalized input also differs in40959 words, max0.005811035633087158.
Thus the mismatch already exists before layer4's SSM computation. Layer4
output differs in all40960 words, max0.03972053527832031. The paired observers
again preserve their respective sampled sequences.

A focused probe of `cuda_dense_ffn_batch_impl` produces no dumps on this
prompt: the suspected standalone FFN callback is not selected. Its observed
and unobserved sequences agree. Its older arithmetic routes are therefore
not established as the cause of this failure. Artifacts:
`/tmp/bitnet-goal-http-ffn3-*`. The temporary probe first failed compilation
because it used assert without an include; replacing that diagnostic check
with an explicit allocation check compiled successfully. Production code
was untouched.

`/tmp/bitnet-goal-http-path.py` records the built-in host-prefill trace at
position7. The default run emits layer3 attention norm, Q/K/V projection,
attention output, WO, residual, FFN norm and gate/up rows. The existing
`BN_CUDA_PREFILL_ATTN_MIN_TOKENS=1` override changes the execution path (those
host trace rows disappear) and changes later generated IDs, but both runs
still match only4/32 reference IDs. This is a failed threshold experiment,
not a correction or accepted parity.

Direct reading of the model's GGUF metadata confirms:
`qwen35.attention.head_count=24`, `head_count_kv=4`, and `key_length=256`.
Its GQA ratio is6. Current `cuda_prefill_attention_mma_enabled` explicitly
accepts only ratios2 and8, so this model cannot select that verified exact
prefill specialization even with the lower threshold. This is a concrete
coverage gap, not proof that attention arithmetic is the only remaining
cause. The next investigation should use independent GGML CUDA attention

Native prototype uses m16n8k64 block-scaled E2M1/E8M0 MMA, zero accumulator
per 64-element fragment, followed by the reference's FP32 fragment and split-K
addition order. A fragment registers must follow ldmatrix.x4 ordering:
row = lane/4 + 8*(register%2), word = lane%4 + 4*(register/2).
The generic tile accessor is not the same mapping. B uses word lane%4+4*reg.
Scales follow the original two-scales-per-register reference layout.
This diagnostic duplicates one input token across all eight B columns and
writes only column zero; optimize to eight distinct compacted tokens before
production use. Shapes with non-512-aligned large K and wider exponent/tie
coverage remain to be tested. No speed claim is made.

several semantics present in src/moe_execute.c decode: routed ffn_sub_norm,

residual branch. These omissions explain a large prefill defect; numerical
rounding differences may remain after restoring the complete architecture.

- src/moe_math.c: router normalization sums float squares in double, rounds
  the mean to float, and applies inverse RMS, inverse sqrt(dim), and router
  scale in sequential multiplication order. New private MoE scale helper
  operates on caller-owned mutable projection outputs.
- src/model_arch.c: Gemma4 no longer sets PREFILL_MATVEC_ROUTER. The explicit
  policy facility remains available for other configurations; ordinary
  prefill now uses the existing contiguous batched router path.
- src/moe_execute.c: mmap, pread (small/large cache), serial CPU fallback and
  serial GPU projection/host-reduction paths keep raw routing coefficients,
  scale expert down outputs first, then route-weight them, then add them.
- src/moe_prefill.c: same scale/route/add ordering and raw route grouping.
  Existing GPU batch APIs accept combined coefficients, so temporary copies
  preserve that callback contract. They are freed before CPU fallback;
  allocation failure skips those callbacks and proceeds with host execution.
  CUDA batch arithmetic still needs separate parity work; this is not its fix.
- src/moe_internal.h: documents the private scaling helper and mutable-owner
  contract. No handles or prepared layouts were added to model weights.
- test/test_moe.c: independent pinned GGML graph goldens check scaled router
  input, NULL scale, in-place use, and expert scale/route/add ordering. Existing
  two-branch synthetic model test also exercises mock CUDA resident-callback
  rejection: it verifies the combined GPU coefficients, then checks that CPU
  fallback still uses raw coefficients and produces the expected output.
