Native implementation:
- Quant registry declares CPU_X86_PACKED_BLOCK32_SUM for Q4_0 (bit49).
- Quant preparation owns the new Q4_0_X8 layout: eight rows per input block,
  original FP16 scales and nibble codes, stored in BnPreparedWeight.aux.
  Eligibility requires positive dimensions, rows divisible by8 and cols by32;
  allocation-size overflow is rejected. Backend model/cache or existing
  transient prepared arenas own the storage. BnQWeight remains immutable and
  contains no backend/prepared handles.
- Format-local AVX2 matvec/matmul and AVX512 VNNI matvec kernels consume that
  layout, sum all32 products in integers, and use explicit per-block FMA.
  Unprepared kernels retain their raw-weight arithmetic. Batch token tiles,
  row task partitioning and caller-owned output buffers remain in place.
- Tied Q4 embedding logits retain the raw-weight path on x86: metadata drives
  backend preparation and logits policy. Runtime orchestration consumes the
  resulting policy flag, including forced CPU-logit acquisition. A synthetic
  test registers a prepared Q4 tensor and verifies tied-logit policy ignores
  it. Other architectures/formats retain their prior preparation policy.

  to prepared K-quant INPUTS has no weight layout and remains unchanged.

Qwen3.8 Flash Next routed Q5_K decode completion (2026-09-11).
The remaining layer-2 midpoint mismatch came from CUDA launch geometry. Pinned
llama.cpp single-token `MUL_MAT_ID` uses four warps per output row for Q5_K:
the 128 threads select blocks with `tid / 16`, advance by eight blocks, retain
`2 * (tid % 16)` as the quant index, fold the other three warp partials into
warp zero lane-by-lane, and finish with an XOR reduction. The previous routed
kernel assigned a complete row to one warp, changing the floating-point sum
tree by one ULP at the observed gate value.

sequential Q5_K-to-native-Q8 expert contract. The batched prompt contract keeps

### Qwen3.8 Flash Next decode: earliest remaining SSM boundary

The expanded no-prefill prompt audit was localized across every prompt
position, rather than only at the eventual token divergence.  For
`In the year 2020, the world`, position 0 remains exact through the observed
layers; the earliest reproducible difference is position 1, layer 4 (an SSM
layer): 698/10240 layer-output floats are bit-exact, with
`max_abs=1.2926757e-6`.  Later positions inherit that state error and first
differ progressively earlier, reaching layer 3 by position 9.

Paired native/llama.cpp captures at position 1, layer 4 establish these exact
input boundaries:

- raw QKV projection: 10240/10240 exact;
- Z projection: 6144/6144 exact;
- sigmoid beta: 48/48 exact;
- recurrent state entering the position: 786432/786432 exact;
- gated SSM output immediately after `SSM_GATE`: 6144/6144 exact.

The last capture used a diagnostic emitter that stopped immediately after the
gate.  A prior 3584/6144 result was not a gate comparison: the following
2560-row output projection had already overwritten the first 2560 entries of
`BN_GPU_VALUE_XB2`.  The same-input recurrent-state comparison is also within
one float rounding step (`max_abs=2.98023224e-8`).  A subsequent paired capture
also proves that the layer-4 Q4_K SSM output projection (6144 columns to 2560
rows) is 2560/2560 bit-exact.  The native Q4_K path uses the pinned llama.cpp
four-warp block distribution and lane-wise partial fold correctly.

The next independent mismatch is in the hyper-connection side state.  The
four-value F32 attention injection projection at layer 4 matches three values;
the fourth differs by one ULP (`-10.0476751328` versus llama.cpp
`-10.0476741791`).  Its input is the wide normalized hyper-connection tensor,

#### 2026-09-15: dense Qwen3.8 default-F32 CUDA decode restored

The canonical dense Qwen3.8 tokenwise year prompt exposed an inverted KV
contract: default F32 bitnet followed the already-exact KV16 trajectory
(token 557), while pinned llama.cpp F32 emitted token 30008. CUDA graph
execution contained a shape-only head-256/GQA6 shortcut that converted F32
K/V attention to the FP16 vector contraction. Removing that obsolete shortcut
restores the ordinary F32 graph path while leaving the dedicated KV16 path
unchanged.

Dense Qwen3.8 now passes 24/24 in both default-F32 batched and tokenwise modes
(`/tmp/q38-dense-f32-final.log`); its KV16 year control passes 3/3. Dense
Qwen3.5 and dense/sparse Qwen3.6 each remain 24/24 in both modes after removal
(`/tmp/q35-dense-no-f32-fused.log`,
`/tmp/q36-after-f32-fused-delete.log`). This removes backend shape inference
rather than adding a model-family condition.
